## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Dhammasaṅgaṇī-anuṭīkā* is a Pali sub-commentary (*anuṭīkā*) belonging to the Abhidhamma sub-commentarial collection (*Tīkā-Abhidhamma*) [Gal 2003; Ronkin 2005]. In the bibliographic tradition of Pali literature, it is also identified as *Abhidhamma-anuṭīkā I* or *Līnatthavaṇṇanā I* [Nyanatusita 2008]. It functions as a secondary commentary on the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī-mūlaṭīkā*, which itself comments upon the *Atthasālinī* (the primary commentary on the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*) [Gal 2003; Nyanatusita 2008; Ronkin 2005]. In modern scholarly studies, sections such as its *Vīsatigāthāvaṇṇanā* have been cited for their refined Abhidhamma doctrinal and semantic distinctions, such as the qualification of *ñeyya* by the word *dhamma* [Dhammajoti 2007].

Textual reuse analyses conducted by DharmaNexus indicate that the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī-anuṭīkā* shares over 26,000 passages across more than 330 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its highest volume of internal reuse occurs with its primary base text, the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī-mūlaṭīkā* (1,329 matches, over 78,000 shared characters), followed by substantial textual parallels with the *Abhidhammāvatāra-purāṇaṭīkā*, the *Majjhimanikāya Mūlapaṇṇāsa-ṭīkā*, the *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā*, the *Abhidhammamātikāpāḷi*, and the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language parallels meeting the match threshold are recorded [DharmaNexus].
